html:
The Football War was a short war between El Salvador and Honduras in July 1969. Riots at World Cup qualifying matches between the two countries set it off, but its causes lay in land and migration.

About 300,000 Salvadorans had moved into Honduras in search of land. A Honduran land reform of 1969 took land from them and expelled many. Tension boiled over during the football games in June, and on 14 July El Salvador invaded.

The war lasted about four days before the Organization of American States arranged a ceasefire. Some thousands died, mostly civilians, and many Salvadorans were forced home. Trade between the two countries stopped, which crippled the Central American Common Market. The return of landless people sharpened the troubles that led to the Salvadoran Civil War a decade later.
sum: The Football War was a short war between El Salvador and Honduras in July 1969. Riots at World Cup qualifying matches between the two countries set it off, but its causes lay in land and migration.
